arxiv-1705-10569.description: A 2017 arXiv research paper by M. Roth and M. Schollmeier. Energetic ions have been observed since the very first laser-plasma experiments. Their origin was found to be the charge separation of electrons heated by the laser, which transfers energy to the ions accelerated in the field. The advent of ultra-intense lasers with pulse lengths in the femtosecond regime resulted in the discovery of very energetic ions with characteristics quite different from those driven by long-pulse lasers.

pmc-12555638.title: Facilitators and barriers for wider implementation of the integrated health care model
pmc-12555638.creator: M Tang, M Veenstra, J Rugkåsa, H Lurås
pmc-12555638.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundHome dwelling frail older adults with complex long-term care needs are a particularly vulnerable group in the healthcare system, facing increased risks of receiving duplicated, fragmented, and uncoordinated care. To address these challenges, Akershus University Hospital, in collaboration with municipalities within its catchment area, has developed and piloted an integrated and person-centred healthcare (IHC) model, aimed at enhancing care coordination across providers, settings and sectors.

pmc-12736172.title: Topical Ozone as an Adjuvant Therapy in Wound Management: An Integrative Review

pmc-12736172.description: Background/Objectives: Wound management remains a clinical challenge, particularly in chronic and refractory conditions. Ozone, due to its antimicrobial, anti-inflammatory, and tissue-regenerative properties, has emerged as promising adjuvant therapy. This integrative re-view aimed to critically analyze the therapeutic effects, routes of administration, benefits, and limitations of ozone in wound treatment.

pmc-13211357.title: Caffeine Exposure Alters Neurotransmission and Stress Physiology in a Freshwater Gastropod
pmc-13211357.creator: Ahlam Mohamed-Benhamu
pmc-13211357.description: Caffeine (CAF) is a widely consumed psychostimulant known to modulate adenosine receptors and neurotransmitter systems, although its effects in invertebrates remain poorly understood. This study examined molecular responses underlying these effects.

pmc-13376142.title: Exosome biogenesis in arthropods: conserved mechanisms, experimental evidence, and emerging directions
pmc-13376142.creator: Festus K Ajibefun, Marija Milosevic, Xiufeng Zhang, Ana M Vélez, Kristopher Silver
pmc-13376142.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoscale, lipid-bound structures released by cells across all domains of life. Once viewed as a means for discarding unwanted cellular components, they are now understood to be central mediators of intercellular communication. Much of what is known about EVs comes from mammalian systems, where extensive work has defined the major EV subtypes and the mechanisms that generate exosomes. These findings continue to serve as the primary reference for interpreting EV biology in other organisms.
